faqs.q: How long does a tile roof last in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: Clay tile lasts 100 years or more and concrete tile a typical 40 to 75 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and the Tile Roofing Industry Alliance, while the underlayment beneath fails first. A 30-to-50-year-old tile roof on a Montclair pre-war home commonly needs new underlayment beneath tiles that remain sound.

faqs.q: Can my Montclair home support the weight of a tile roof?

runs.v: A tile roof loads the framing well above an asphalt roof, so a structural assessment confirms the framing carries the tile before installation. Strengthening rafters, trusses, or ridge beams to carry it triggers a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and Newark Quality Roofing assesses the structure first.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for tile roof work in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: Permits are typically required for significant roofing work in Montclair, but not for everything. A re-roof or repair of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. On commercial or multi-family buildings, work beyond 25% of the roof in 12 months, or any structural change, needs a permit, so confirm with the Montclair construction office; a permitted re-roof removes the existing tile rather than covering over it, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

faqs.q: How much does roof tile replacement cost on a 2,000-square-foot house?

runs.v: Roof area, not floor area, sets the price, because pitch and overhangs add square footage. Tile costs more per square foot than asphalt, so it typically runs toward or above the top of the $10,000–$25,000 New Jersey range, and a free written estimate prices the measured roof.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: In New Jersey it is a permit threshold, not a rule that forces a full replacement: on buildings other than detached one- and two-family homes, repairing up to 25% of the roof in any 12 months is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and more needs a permit.
